result.proposed_fix: (1) snapshot.js: build field labels only from text nodes that pass textVisible() inside label[for], the wrapping label and aria-labelledby targets, and emit them as label pieces with rects (pieces.labels[i]). Stop emitting aria-label, name, id and placeholder as display text (send them only to the in-page sensitivity test). Never emit a label for a field that is not shown (count it instead). (2) perception.normalise: run onscreen.keep on label pieces like headings; a field whose label is not drawn keeps type/required/has_value and gets a neutral name ('text field N'). bridge._context_block must not fall back to name/id. (3) onscreen.py: tie the check to the text at least for stacked text, by dropping any piece whose rects overlap another piece's rects beyond a small fraction (or, in-page, any text node that is not the topmost at its rect centre via elementsFromPoint, including when the hit element is its own ancestor). Otherwise state in docs that overlapping-ink text is unverified and stop labelling it 'pixel-checked'. (4) Add a self-contained Chromium regression test (embed the probe page: sr-only label, aria-label, aria-labelledby to hidden span, name-only input, type=hidden aria-label, z-index:-1 and white text over a visible line; with and without Ctrl+A; real screenshot) that asserts no *-PAYLOAD string appears in FakeClient.bodies and that visible text still does. (5) Correct docs/assist/03 and A0_QUALIFICATION to list the field-label channel and the remaining limits exactly.
result.root_cause: At HEAD fcfb465 the boundary against hidden page text (owner decision D10) covers only snapshot.pieces (page text, selection, headings), and its pixel test checks only that some ink exists inside a piece's rectangles. Two defects follow. (1) Unchecked channel: form-field labels are built in snapshot.js labelOf() from label.innerText (which keeps screen-reader-only clip, transparent and other undrawn text), aria-labelledby targets' innerText (even for [hidden] elements) and the aria-label attribute. bridge._context_block also falls back to the name and id attributes. All of these go to the Brain under 'Form fields' with no visibility check and no pixel check. Fields that are not shown but count as sensitive (type=hidden) are kept with their labels. (2) Pixel test not tied to the text: onscreen.Screen.check counts horizontal colour edges in the rectangle, so hidden text placed over visible text (z-index:-1 under the ancestor's background, or white on white without a selection) passes because of the other text's ink and is sent labelled 'pixel-checked'. Real Chromium probe (/tmp/uri_diag_D7/probe.py, mk/grant/ask_and_wait, real screenshot): status COMPLETE; the Brain body contains LABELSR-PAYLOAD (the R11 sr-only clip:rect technique, as a <label>), ARIALABEL-PAYLOAD, ARIALB-PAYLOAD (span hidden), NAMEATTR-PAYLOAD and HIDDENINPUT-PAYLOAD under 'Form fields', and ZOVER-PAYLOAD under 'On-screen text (pixel-checked)' and 'Selected text (pixel-checked)'; WHITEOVER-PAYLOAD as well without a selection. redactions={} without a selection and {'selection_withheld': 1} after Ctrl+A. None of these payloads is readable in the screenshots, except WHITEOVER once the Ctrl+A highlight repaints it.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: d5a9b41 (R11) and d029f60 (R12) each extended the in-page list of CSS hiding techniques and tested only the payloads the reviewer had named (12 and 24 PAYLOAD lines in their tests); every later round found techniques outside the list (R12: filter/text-fill/clip-path shapes/mask/details; R13: negative z-index under the ancestor's background, SVG fill, -webkit-mask-box-image). fcfb465 (D10) changed the approach to a screenshot pixel check, but applied it only to the new pieces arrays. Field labels, aria-label, aria-labelledby, name and id, which also carry page-authored text to the Brain, were left on the old path, which has no per-text visibility check at all (labelOf uses innerText and attributes). The pixel check also measures ink in the rectangle rather than ink belonging to the text, so overlapping visible ink vouches for hidden text. D10 documented this as residual L-A0-5, yet the text is still labelled 'pixel-checked'. The D10 test page (test_a0_d10_pixel_checked_text.py PAGE) has no form fields and no hidden text placed over visible text, so neither gap was exercised.
